### 🔵 Needs a closer look The breaking-change migration table currently directs users to selectors that unnecessarily disable unrelated instrumentation. **0 open findings**
Previously missed (2) In code that hasn't changed since last review
Replacement mappings broaden service-specific instrumentation scope `CHANGELOG.md:25` [Config] These replacements broaden service-specific controls to the whole SDK version. The new modules retain `aws-sdk-sqs`, `aws-sdk-sns`, `aws-sdk-lambda`, and `aws-sdk-bedrock-runtime`, so users following this table would disable unrelated AWS SDK instrumentation. Map each removed service selector to its corresponding feature selector; only the `*-core` aliases should map to the versioned component.
Migration targets broaden scope beyond removed selectors `CHANGELOG.md:28` [Config] These migration targets are broader than the removed selectors: `camel-2.20` also controls non-JMS Camel modules, while the two versioned ClickHouse names require duplicating what was previously one shared setting. The retained `camel-jms` and `clickhouse-client` selectors target the same module groups as the removed aliases, so those are the direct replacements.

<!--

Use versioned-first Java agent instrumentation names unconditionally and remove legacy and implementation-only enablement aliases. Part of #20510.

```properties
# Before
otel.instrumentation.cxf-3.2.enabled=false
# After
otel.instrumentation.jaxrs-2.0-cxf-3.2.enabled=false
```

Versioned component selectors now take precedence over role, versionless, and umbrella selectors. Shared component selectors control all of their implementations; CHANGELOG.md lists replacements and changed umbrella membership.

Removes the internal `DeprecatedInstrumentationNames` extension helper. Emitted scope names and declarative selector spelling changes are separate PRs.
metadata.title: Use versioned-first instrumentation names and remove legacy aliases
